$comment: Which control a decision may be asked for in — written once, read twice.
This is the knowledge, not the mechanism. `skills.py` renders it into the
system prompt so the model is taught it, and `controls.py` checks compiled
surfaces against the same rows so a turn that ignores the teaching is
rewritten before anyone sees it. Editing the table changes both, which is
the point: a rule stated in a prompt and enforced by a separate hand-kept
list is two rules that drift.
`Text` is allowed everywhere: reading a decision back is not asking for one,
and a panel that says '12-19 April' as text is correct.

controls.instead: a DateRangePicker bound to both dates
controls.why: a text box accepts "next tuesday", "12/4" and "April 12ish", and then the trip is priced for the wrong week

controls.instead: a DateRangePicker bound to both dates
controls.why: the end of a trip is the other half of one question, not a second one

controls.instead: a ChoicePicker of the departure airports this deployment serves
controls.why: the answer is one of twenty-one airports; pills make picking one tap and typing a code that does not exist impossible

controls.instead: a ChoicePicker of the destinations this deployment has
controls.why: there are nine, and naming a tenth is a failed lookup two turns later
a party size is a small whole number, and a counter is how you say that
there are four, and they have names the traveller recognises
a budget is a feeling about a range, and a slider is the control that says so
a cap is a point on a range they can see
it is yes or no, per stop
